mappings.note: The onset of the reproductive phase in women is a human reproduction process, which LO-80 names verbatim. Not LO-87, because nothing is applied to daily living.
The right meal for an adolescent is science applied to daily life, the adolescence strand of LO-87. Not LO-80, because no bodily process is explained.
Sex determination by the XX combination is part of explaining human reproduction. Not LO-77, whose reproduction example is the sexual/asexual split.
The XY combination is the same mechanism for the other case. The frame offers no finer distinction between the two.
The human chromosome count underpins the sex-determination explanation. Not LO-83, which needs slides prepared and described.
Identifying an iron-rich food is a dietary choice made in daily life. Not LO-79, because no cause-and-effect is traced.
Which gland makes adrenaline is part of explaining endocrine control in the body. The frame has one outcome for human physiology, so this recall cluster shares it.
A Y-bearing sperm determining the zygote's sex is the fertilisation mechanism. Not the competency-level code, since a learning outcome fits.
Hormones controlling the changes of adolescence is the causal explanation of a body process. Not LO-87, because nothing is acted on.
Recognising a balanced diet is an everyday application of nutrition. Not LO-80, which covers processes inside the body.
The legal age of marriage belongs to the social side of adolescence LO-87 names, including myths and taboos. Not LO-80, because it is not a biological process.
Attributing AIDS to a virus relates a phenomenon to its cause. Not LO-77, because no microorganisms are sorted into classes.
Hormone transport by the bloodstream is a body process to explain. Not LO-84, which needs a labelled diagram.
Where hormones are produced is part of the endocrine explanation. Shares the outcome with the rest of this recall cluster.
The pituitary as master gland describes how endocrine control is organised. No classification outcome covers glands.
Pancreas-to-insulin is gland-to-secretion recall inside the endocrine explanation. The frame provides no more specific outcome.
Insulin regulating blood sugar is a physiological regulation mechanism. Not LO-79, whose causal examples are environmental.
Linking goitre to iodine deficiency relates a condition to its cause. Deliberately different from the gland-recall items, which describe a working process.
Endocrine glands secreting hormones is the defining statement of the endocrine process. Kept at the outcome rather than the competency because the outcome covers processes in humans.
Naming a pituitary hormone continues the endocrine strand. No sibling fits, the classification outcomes covering materials and organisms.
Iodine as the element thyroxine needs is part of how the thyroid works. Not LO-79, because the item asks the composition, not the deficiency effect.
Thyroid-to-thyroxine is gland-to-secretion recall. Shares the outcome with its neighbours.
Adrenaline acting in fear and excitement is the emergency response mechanism. Not LO-87, because no daily decision follows.
Menarche as the first menstruation is a reproductive event in humans. Not LO-87, which would fit hygiene or myth-busting advice.
Menopause as the end of the reproductive phase mirrors the menarche item. One outcome serves both.
Puberty defined by the onset of reproductive maturity is a human process. Not LO-87, because no myth or practice is engaged.
Why adolescents must watch their diet turns nutrition into a decision about one's own body. Chosen over LO-80 because the practical consequence is the point.
Adolescence as the period of transition to maturity describes a stage of human development. Not LO-87, because no application follows.
An X-bearing sperm giving a girl is the sex-determination mechanism. Grouped with the other chromosome items.
How many chromosome pairs humans have underpins sex determination. Not LO-83, because no slide is described.
Children gaining height during puberty is a growth change of adolescence. Not LO-76, because no male/female contrast is drawn.
Testes secreting testosterone is gland-to-secretion recall within the endocrine explanation. Not LO-84, because the secretion rather than the organ is the answer.

The Adam's apple as the enlarged voice box in boys is a secondary sexual characteristic that tells the sexes apart, which is differentiation by structure. Not LO-80, reserved here for the processes rather than the distinguishing features.
Hormones as the secretions of endocrine glands is the defining statement of the endocrine process. Duplicate in substance of the earlier item.
What determines the baby's sex is the sex-determination mechanism. Grouped with the chromosome items.
The stoppage of menstruation being menopause is a reproductive event. Duplicate in substance of the menopause item.
The adrenal hormone is gland-to-secretion recall. Grouped with the endocrine cluster.
The onset of the reproductive phase in women is a human reproduction process. Duplicate of the first item in this chapter.
The testes as the male gonads names a reproductive organ, which LO-84 covers with the human reproductive organs. Not LO-80, which is used where a secretion or process is asked for.
